definition: John von Neumann (Hungarian: Neumann János Lajos; December 28, 1903 – February 8, 1957) was a Hungarian and American mathematician, physicist, computer scientist and engineer.
details: Computer architecture, cellular automata and early thinking on self-reproducing machines and neural computation. Von Neumann had perhaps the widest breadth of any mathematician of his time, integrating pure and applied sciences and making major contributions to many fields, including mathematics, physics, economics, computing, and statistics. He was a pioneer in building the mathematical framework of quantum physics, in the development of functional analysis, and in game theory, introducing or codifying concepts including cellular automata, the universal constructor and the digital computer.

explainer.lead: John von Neumann was a Hungarian and American mathematician and physicist (1903–1957). His work spans functional analysis, operator theory, mathematics and physics.
explainer.knownFor: He was known for always being happy to provide others of all ability levels with scientific and mathematical advice.

contributions.name: He developed the mathematical models behind the explosive lenses used in the implosion-type nuclear weapon.
He played a key role alongside Bernard Schriever and Trevor Gardner in the design and development of the United States' first intercontinental ballistic missile (ICBM) programs.
Von Neumann's contributions and intellectual ability drew praise from colleagues in physics, mathematics, and beyond.
His daughter wrote that he was very concerned with his legacy in two aspects: his life and the durability of his intellectual contributions to the world.
His pioneering papers with Subrahmanyan Chandrasekhar on the statistics of a fluctuating gravitational field generated by randomly distributed stars were considered a tour de force.

timeline.what: Joins Armed Forces Special Weapons Project (until 1955)
Commissioner at United States Atomic Energy Commission (until 1957)
Receives the Carl-Gustaf Rossby Research Medal
Receives the Financial Times Person of the Year
